terra.problem: The verse says the creditors will arise, not that nobody forgets the debt.
The verse does not say what the creditors remember or forget; it says they will arise.
The comparison to a cookie with no dough does not make sense or clearly match building a house by unjust gain.
The claim that honest gain would mean there would be no woe goes beyond what the verse says.
‘He's building bigger now’ adds a sequence of events. The passage gives woes about a house and a city but does not say one was built after the other.
The passage does not say the proud man wanted gold. It also says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD's glory, not simply His glory.
‘He wanted to look big’ gives him a motive the text does not state.
The explanation is flat and generic, doing little beyond ruling out Egypt and naming Lebanon.

‘What he did’ attributes the destruction of the animals to the proud man, but the text does not say who destroyed them.
The explanation is generic and merely repeats that the temple is the place named.
